title: Conferment of Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) & Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards (Akademi Puraskar) for the years 2024 and 2025
body_text:
The Hon’ble President of India will confer the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships and Awards for the years 2024 and 2025 to 115 artists in a special investiture ceremony scheduled for Thursday, 13 August 2026 at 11:30 a.m. at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat , Hon’ble Minister for Culture and Tourism, Govt. of India, Shri Rao Inderjit Singh, Hon’ble Minister of State for Planning, Statistics, and Programme Implementation (Independent Charge) and Hon’ble Minister of State for Culture, Govt. of India, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India and Dr Sandhya Purecha, Chairman, Sangeet Natak Akademi will grace the award ceremony. The Fellows and Awardees so selected represent the nation as a whole, and belong to different States and Union Territories of India.  Besides, these eminent artists cover  the  entire gamut of the performing art forms expressed in the form of music, dance, drama, folk & tribal art, puppetry and allied theatre art forms, etc. The Akademi Awards have been conferred since 1952.  These honours not only symbolize the highest standard of excellence and achievement, but also recognize sustained individual work and contribution.  The honour of Akademi Fellow carries a purse money of Rs. 3,00,000/- (Rupees three lakh only) while the Akademi Award carries a purse money of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees  one lakh only), besides a Tamrapatra and Angavastram. The list of 115 artists selected for the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards is attached in Annexure-1. enrichment.summary: The President of India will confer Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships (Akademi Ratna) and Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards (Akademi Puraskar) for 2024 and 2025 upon 115 artists at a ceremony on 13 August 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The honourees span music, dance, theatre, folk/tribal arts, puppetry and allied art forms from across India's States and Union Territories. Fellows receive Rs 3 lakh purse money while Awardees receive Rs 1 lakh, along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram, continuing a tradition of Akademi Awards conferred since 1952.
enrichment.context: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, is the oldest of the country's national academies of art (set up in 1952) and functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture. Its Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) and Awards (Akademi Puraskar) are the highest official recognitions for performing artists in India, aimed at honouring sustained excellence and contribution across classical, folk, tribal and experimental art forms. These awards are significant for cultural policy discussions as they help preserve and promote India's intangible cultural heritage, including lesser-known folk and tribal traditions from states like Nagaland, Ladakh, Mizoram and Jharkhand alongside classical traditions like Hindustani and Carnatic music, Bharatanatyam, Kathak and Kathakali. The event also reflects the government's soft-power and cultural diplomacy efforts, and ties into broader schemes for safeguarding traditional art forms, artisan communities, and the Guru-Shishya parampara. Such recognitions often feature in current affairs for Prelims (institutional facts, awardee fields) and are useful in Mains answers on cultural heritage preservation, diversity, and the role of autonomous cultural institutions in nation-building.

prelims_questions.question: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, which confers the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship) and Akademi Puraskar (Awards), is the national academy for which of the following fields?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama (performing arts), and has been conferring these awards since 1952.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the Sangeet Natak Akademi honours, consider the following statements: 1. The Akademi Fellowship carries a higher purse money than the Akademi Award. 2. Both honours include a Tamrapatra and Angavastram. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the Fellowship carries Rs 3 lakh while the Award carries Rs 1 lakh, and both include a Tamrapatra and Angavastram.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of national academies like the Sangeet Natak Akademi in preserving India's diverse performing art traditions, including folk and tribal art forms. What challenges do such traditions face in contemporary India?

Autonomous cultural institutions play a vital role in India's soft power and heritage preservation. Examine the significance of state recognition (such as national awards) in sustaining traditional art forms and the livelihoods of artists.
